newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Good corporate results lift Nigerian share trade.
newsitem.headline: Good corporate results lift Nigerian share trade.

text.p: Improved corporate results on Wednesday helped boost trading on the Nigerian stock market, further pushing higher the all-share index.
It closed at 7070.63 from 7061.91 on Tuesday when gainers overwhelmingly outnumbered losers, traders said.
Strong three-month profits at Guinness to end-September 1996 breathed some confidence into the troubled brewery sector although the stock itself closed unchanged at 8.21 naira.
The company reported an after-tax profit of 132.8 million naira against 110.5 million naira in the previous year.
Industrial Gases surged 55 kobo to 11.55 naira on the announcement of a good full-year result to end-September 1996.
Profit after taxation rose to 81.1 million naira from 51.6 million naira in 1995.
News that conglomerate UAC had acquired controlling shares in a multi-purpose mill and a company producing mineral water caused its price to rise 15 kobo to 7.85 naira.
But fellow conglomerate Lever Brothers tumbled to 19.00 naira, down 63 kobo, due to glut of its stock in the market.

Cement shares continued to drift. Ashaka and Benue Cement slid to 15.90 naira and 6.90 naira, down 20 kobo and 10 kobo, respectively. But sectoral leader West African Portland Cement remained in strong demand, closing 15 kobo more at 48.40 naira.
Chemical and Allied Products took a five kobo tumble as investors continued to sell on its recent poor performances.
Food and petroleum marketing shares were higher on demand.
Nestle Foods and Coca-Cola bottlers Nigerian Bottling company led their sector, gaining 15 kobo to 51.35 naira and 21 kobo to 31.11 naira, respectively, traders said.
Unipetrol advanced to 62.00 naira, up 39 kobo.
Mobil was 51 kobo stronger at 51.81 naira while Total finished at 59.85 naira, up 25 kobo.
